questions.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order in the dataset (99,441), whatever its status. It does not exclude canceled or unavailable orders.

questions.question: How many sellers are on the platform?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sellers
FROM sellers
questions.note: This counts every seller registered in the sellers table (3,095), whether or not they have made a sale.

questions.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviews
FROM order_reviews
questions.note: This averages every row in order_reviews, which has one row per review-order pair, so a few reviews that cover several orders are counted once per order.

questions.question: What is the total value of all payments in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_payments
FROM order_payments
questions.note: Because the question asks about all payments in the dataset, this sums every payment row, including those on canceled and unavailable orders, with no sales-status filter.

questions.question: What is the average price of an order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2) AS avg_item_price,
  COUNT(*)                AS items
FROM order_items oi
questions.note: This averages `price` (excluding freight) over all order item rows (one row per unit), without filtering on order status.

questions.question: How many products are there in each product category (English names)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS products
FROM products
GROUP BY COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY products DESC, category
questions.note: This counts catalog products per English category, and products with no category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: How many distinct orders used each payment type?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status. One order can use several payment types, so it can appear in more than one row and the counts add up to more than the total number of orders.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders have the status delivered?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') / COUNT(*), 2) AS delivered_pct
FROM orders
questions.note: The denominator is every order in the table, including all statuses such as canceled and unavailable.

questions.question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments,
    COUNT(*)                            AS credit_card_payments
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'
questions.note: This averages over every credit card payment row, with no filter on order status.

questions.question: What is the average order value, measured as total payment per order, for orders that were not canceled or unavailable?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT op.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) AS total_paid
    FROM order_payments op
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY op.order_id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(total_paid), 2) AS total_payments,
    ROUND(SUM(total_paid) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM order_pay
questions.note: Average order value is total payments divided by the number of distinct sale orders that have at least one payment row.

questions.question: What is the median total payment per order, across all orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SUM(payment_value) AS total_paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_paid)::numeric, 2) AS median_payment_per_order,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM order_totals
questions.note: I read "across all orders" literally. The query includes every order with a payment record, regardless of status, so canceled and unavailable orders are not excluded.

questions.question: How many unique customers live in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers_rj
FROM customers
WHERE customer_state = 'RJ'
questions.note: This counts distinct people (customer_unique_id) with an RJ address on any of their orders, including orders of every status.

questions.question: How many products weigh more than 10 kg?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_over_10kg
FROM products
WHERE product_weight_g > 10000
questions.note: This counts products in the catalog whose recorded weight is strictly greater than 10,000 g; products with no recorded weight (NULL) are excluded.

questions.question: How many order items cost more than 1,000 BRL?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_over_1000
FROM order_items
WHERE price > 1000
questions.note: This counts every order item (unit) whose price, excluding freight, is above 1,000 BRL, across all order statuses, because the question doesn't limit it to sales.

questions.question: How many delivered orders arrived after their estimated delivery date?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
questions.note: This counts delivered orders that have a delivery date and arrived after the estimated date, following the late-delivery rule. The expected result is about 7,827.

questions.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sp_sellers
FROM sellers
WHERE seller_state = 'SP'
questions.note: This counts every registered seller whose `seller_state` is 'SP', whether or not they have made any sales.

questions.question: How many 1-star reviews include a comment message?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'reviews'
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) FILTER (
    WHERE review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
      AND btrim(review_comment_message) <> ''
  ) AS one_star_with_comment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) AS one_star_total,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) FILTER (
      WHERE review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
        AND btrim(review_comment_message) <> ''
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT review_id), 0),
    2
  ) AS pct_with_comment
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_score = 1
questions.note: I counted distinct review_id, because one review can cover several orders, and I treated blank messages as having no comment.

questions.question: How many distinct orders were paid at least partly with a voucher?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS voucher_orders
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'voucher'
questions.note: This counts every order with at least one voucher payment row, regardless of order status. Canceled and unavailable orders are included because the question is about payment method, not sales.

questions.question: How many products have no category?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category
FROM products
WHERE product_category_name_english IS NULL
questions.note: This counts catalog products whose English category name is NULL, meaning the category is unknown. The documentation puts this at 610 products, about 1.9% of the catalog.

questions.question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_seller_orders
FROM (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1
) t
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status (the dataset notes give 1,278).

questions.question: List the cities in the state of Acre (AC) with the number of unique customers in each.
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'AC'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
questions.note: This counts distinct people (customer_unique_id) across all orders in Acre, regardless of order status.

questions.question: How many orders were approved more than 24 hours after they were placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_approved_after_24h
FROM orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp > INTERVAL '24 hours'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status that have an approval time more than 24 hours after purchase; orders with no approval time are left out.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    s.seller_state AS state,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue,
    COUNT(*) AS units_sold,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue per seller is the sum of item prices without freight, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: What is the total revenue by customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (payments, including freight and installment interest), counting only sales orders, which excludes canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which customer state has the highest average freight value per order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state                AS state,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight_per_item,
    COUNT(*)                        AS items
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY avg_freight_per_item DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted only sales orders, so canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and each order_items row is treated as one item.

questions.question: How many orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, because the question asks about orders placed, not completed sales.

questions.question: Which 10 cities have the most unique customers?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city                     AS city,
    c.customer_state                    AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I grouped by city and state together because some city names exist in more than one state, and I counted people with `customer_unique_id` across all orders regardless of order status.

questions.question: What is the average review score of orders paid with each payment type?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay_types AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, payment_type
    FROM order_payments
),
order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS order_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    p.payment_type,
    COUNT(*)                         AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(s.order_score), 2)     AS avg_review_score
FROM order_pay_types p
JOIN order_scores s ON s.order_id = p.order_id
GROUP BY p.payment_type
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
questions.note: Each order is counted once per payment type it used, so an order paid with a voucher and a card counts in both groups. An order with several reviews contributes its mean score. All order statuses are included, and orders without a review are excluded.

questions.question: What was the total freight charged on items in the furniture_decor category?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'total_freight'
questions.sql:
SELECT
    ROUND(SUM(oi.freight_value), 2) AS total_freight,
    COUNT(*)                        AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders   o ON o.order_id   = oi.order_id
WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'furniture_decor'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: This treats freight as a sales measure, so it leaves out canceled and unavailable orders; drop the status filter if you want freight on every item ever listed.

questions.question: What was the total revenue from customers in Minas Gerais (MG)?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS mg_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.customer_state = 'MG'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: Revenue here is the total of what customers paid (`order_payments.payment_value`), the default for order-level totals; canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: What is the English name of the product category 'cama_mesa_banho'?
questions.sql:
SELECT product_category_name AS category_pt,
       product_category_name_english AS category_en
FROM category_translation
WHERE product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
questions.note: This looks up the Portuguese name in the translation table (it should return bed_bath_table).

questions.question: Which product category has the highest average review score among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
order_categories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders,
       ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM order_categories oc
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Each order counts once per category, using the average of its reviews, and orders of every status are included.

questions.question: Which 3 sellers have the highest average review score among sellers with at least 50 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS order_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id
    FROM order_items
)
SELECT
    so.seller_id,
    s.seller_state,
    COUNT(*) AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(os.order_score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_orders so
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = so.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = so.seller_id
GROUP BY so.seller_id, s.seller_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
ORDER BY AVG(os.order_score) DESC, COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 3
questions.note: Each review counts once per seller-order pair, and orders with several reviews are first averaged to one score per order; orders of every status are included.

questions.question: How many unique customers bought from a seller located in a different state from their own?
questions.sql:
WITH buyer_flags AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        BOOL_OR(s.seller_state <> c.customer_state) AS bought_cross_state
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c   ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN sellers s     ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE bought_cross_state)                         AS cross_state_customers,
    COUNT(*)                                                           AS total_customers,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE bought_cross_state) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_cross_state
FROM buyer_flags
questions.note: This counts people by customer_unique_id, using only orders that count as sales (not canceled or unavailable). A customer is counted if at least one item they bought came from a seller in a different state from their own.

questions.question: What is the average price of items sold by sellers in each seller state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    s.seller_state                 AS seller_state,
    COUNT(*)                       AS units_sold,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)        AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders  o ON o.order_id  = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY avg_item_price DESC
questions.note: This averages the unit price (excluding freight) over all items from orders that count as sales, meaning canceled and unavailable orders are left out.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each year?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed, whatever its status, by purchase year. Coverage is partial for two years: 2016 has only Sep–Dec, and those months are sparse, while 2018 effectively ends in August.

questions.question: Which month had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed in each month, including canceled and unavailable ones, and uses the purchase timestamp to assign the month.

questions.question: What was the average review score for each month of 2018, based on when the review was created?
questions.sql:
WITH reviews AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (review_id)
           review_id,
           review_score,
           review_creation_date
    FROM order_reviews
    WHERE review_creation_date >= DATE '2018-01-01'
      AND review_creation_date <  DATE '2019-01-01'
    ORDER BY review_id, review_creation_date
)
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', review_creation_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS review_month,
    COUNT(*)                                                       AS reviews,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score)::numeric, 2)                           AS avg_score
FROM reviews
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', review_creation_date)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', review_creation_date)
questions.note: Each review is counted once, even when it covers several orders, and no order-status filter is applied. The order feed effectively ends in August 2018, so the review counts for September and October 2018 will be thin and their averages less reliable.

questions.question: What was the total revenue in Q4 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_q4_2017
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-10-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue is the total paid by customers (payment_value) for orders placed from October to December 2017, excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: On which day of the week (e.g. Monday) are the most orders placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    TO_CHAR(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay') AS weekday,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
GROUP BY TO_CHAR(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay')
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed, whatever its status, because the question is about when orders are placed rather than about sales.

questions.question: For each purchase month of 2017, what was the average delivery time in days (as a decimal) for delivered orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS purchase_month,
  COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: Delivery time is measured in fractional days from purchase to customer delivery, and each order is grouped by the month it was purchased.

questions.question: How many orders were placed on Black Friday 2017 (November 24, 2017)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS orders_placed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS sales_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-11-24'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2017-11-25'
questions.note: `orders_placed` counts every order regardless of status, and `sales_orders` leaves out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule.

questions.question: Which product category had the largest increase in units sold from January–August 2017 to January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2017-09-01'
        ) AS units_2017,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
        ) AS units_2018
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    units_2017,
    units_2018,
    units_2018 - units_2017 AS unit_increase
FROM units
ORDER BY unit_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts units sold (order_items rows) in each January–August window and excludes canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which month of 2018 had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted orders as sales, so canceled and unavailable orders are excluded; 2018 data ends in August (September and October are nearly empty), so only Jan–Aug really compete.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories had the largest drop in revenue from July 2018 to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-08-01') AS jul_rev,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01') AS aug_rev
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(COALESCE(jul_rev, 0), 2) AS jul_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(aug_rev, 0), 2) AS aug_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(jul_rev, 0) - COALESCE(aug_rev, 0), 2) AS revenue_drop,
    ROUND(100.0 * (COALESCE(jul_rev, 0) - COALESCE(aug_rev, 0)) / NULLIF(jul_rev, 0), 2) AS drop_pct
FROM cat_month
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue here means item sales (SUM of price, without freight) from orders that are not canceled or unavailable, and a category with no August sales counts as 0.

questions.question: What was the month-over-month percentage change in the number of orders for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
changes AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS mom_pct_change
FROM changes
WHERE month >= '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, and it includes December 2017 so that January 2018 has a prior month to compare against.

questions.question: For each customer state, which product category generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_state AS state,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_state, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        category,
        revenue,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM cat_rev
)
SELECT
    state,
    category AS top_category,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY state
questions.note: Revenue here is the sum of item prices without freight, because the breakdown is by category, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded; if two categories tie in a state, both are shown.

questions.question: What was the 3-month moving average of monthly revenue for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
ma AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        revenue,
        AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_3m
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT
    to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    ROUND(moving_avg_3m, 2) AS moving_avg_3m
FROM ma
WHERE month >= DATE '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: Revenue is payments (SUM of payment_value), excluding canceled and unavailable orders. The moving average is trailing: the current month plus the two before it, so January 2018 includes November and December 2017.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers had the highest item revenue in 2018, and what percentage of total 2018 item revenue did each account for?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'

)
SELECT sr.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       ROUND(sr.revenue, 2) AS item_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * sr.revenue / SUM(sr.revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_2018_revenue
FROM seller_rev sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
ORDER BY sr.revenue DESC

questions.question: For 2017 and 2018 separately, what were the top 3 product categories by units sold?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_units AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS yr,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) AS units_sold
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        yr,
        category,
        units_sold,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY yr ORDER BY units_sold DESC) AS rnk
    FROM cat_units
)
SELECT yr AS year, rnk AS rank, category, units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY year, rank
questions.note: Units are order_items rows from orders that are not canceled or unavailable, assigned to a year by purchase date. Ties can return more than 3 rows per year. 2018 effectively covers only January to August, plus a few orders in September and October.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders came from each customer state?

FROM orders o

questions.question: Which month in 2017 had the largest increase in orders compared with the previous month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
diffs AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders,
           orders - LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS increase,
           ROUND(100.0 * (orders - LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month))
                 / NULLIF(LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS pct_increase
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       increase,
       pct_increase
FROM diffs
WHERE prev_orders IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all placed orders regardless of status and compares only February to December 2017. January is left out because December 2016 had just one order, which would make January's increase an artificial spike.

questions.question: For each seller state, which seller has the highest revenue?

ranked AS (

    FROM seller_rev

SELECT seller_state AS state,
       seller_id AS top_seller,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1

questions.note: Revenue is the sum of item prices (no freight) from orders that are not canceled or unavailable, and ties within a state are all shown.

questions.question: How are we doing?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
rev AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
base AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_status,
        c.customer_unique_id,
        p.paid,
        r.score,
        o.order_delivered_customer_date,
        o.order_estimated_delivery_date
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)                         AS orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id)               AS customers,
        SUM(paid)                                        AS revenue,
        AVG(score)                                       AS avg_review,
        AVG(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
            FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
                      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) AS late_rate
    FROM base
    GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
    month,
    orders,
    customers,
    ROUND(revenue, 2)                                         AS revenue,
    ROUND(revenue / orders, 2)                                AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS revenue_mom_pct,
    ROUND(avg_review, 2)                                      AS avg_review,
    ROUND(100 * late_rate, 2)                                 AS late_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
questions.note:
Since "how are we doing" is open-ended, this query returns a monthly KPI scorecard. It covers revenue, orders, average order value, unique customers, review score, late-delivery rate and month-over-month revenue growth.

Assumptions: revenue means payments, sales exclude canceled and unavailable orders, and the window is limited to the reliable months 2017-01 to 2018-08.

questions.question: Who are our best customers?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
cust AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        MAX(c.customer_state)             AS state,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)        AS orders,
        SUM(op.paid)                      AS total_spent,
        MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp)   AS first_purchase,
        MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp)   AS last_purchase
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
    customer_unique_id                    AS customer,
    state,
    orders,
    ROUND(total_spent, 2)                 AS total_spent,
    ROUND(total_spent / orders, 2)        AS avg_order_value,
    first_purchase::date                  AS first_purchase,
    last_purchase::date                   AS last_purchase
FROM cust
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I took "best customers" to mean the top 10 people by total amount paid. People are identified by customer_unique_id, spend is the sum of payments, and canceled or unavailable orders are excluded. If a person ordered from more than one state, the state column shows just one of them.

questions.question: What is the age distribution of our customers?
questions.sql:
WITH first_purchase AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_ts
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
ref AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS ref_ts FROM orders
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT CASE
             WHEN f.first_ts > r.ref_ts - INTERVAL '3 months'  THEN '1: < 3 months'
             WHEN f.first_ts > r.ref_ts - INTERVAL '6 months'  THEN '2: 3-6 months'
             WHEN f.first_ts > r.ref_ts - INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '3: 6-12 months'
             WHEN f.first_ts > r.ref_ts - INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '4: 12-24 months'
             ELSE '5: 24+ months'
           END AS tenure_bucket
    FROM first_purchase f
    CROSS JOIN ref r
)
SELECT tenure_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_customers
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY tenure_bucket
ORDER BY tenure_bucket
questions.note:
There is no age or birth-date column in the database, so demographic age can't be computed. As a proxy, this query shows **customer tenure**: how long ago each person first bought, measured against the last purchase date in the data.

Tenure is measured against the last purchase timestamp, which falls in Oct 2018 when the data feed was already sparse. This means the "< 3 months" bucket will look smaller than it really is.

questions.question: What percentage of unique customers have placed more than one order?
questions.sql:
WITH per_person AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders
    FROM orders o

questions.question: How many orders have a total payment that differs from the sum of their items' price plus freight by more than 1 BRL?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
items AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(price + freight_value) AS item_total
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(p.paid - i.item_total) > 1) AS mismatched_orders,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_compared,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(p.paid - i.item_total) > 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS mismatch_pct
FROM pay p
JOIN items i ON i.order_id = p.order_id
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, but only those that have both payment rows and item rows, since orders missing either cannot be compared.

    ))::numeric, 2) AS median_delivery_days,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'

GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY median_delivery_days DESC

questions.question: What was the total revenue from orders that include at least one bed_bath_table item?

       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)     AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND EXISTS (

        FROM order_items oi

questions.question: What were the total revenue and the total freight for each customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH sales_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_state
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
frt AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(freight_value) AS freight
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    s.customer_state                         AS state,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(p.paid, 0)), 2)       AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(f.freight, 0)), 2)    AS total_freight
FROM sales_orders s
LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = s.order_id
LEFT JOIN frt f ON f.order_id = s.order_id
GROUP BY s.customer_state
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue is the default order-level measure, total payments, which already include freight. Freight comes from order_items. Each source is aggregated per order before joining to avoid fan-out, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

JOIN sellers s   ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state

    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)    AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c   ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN sellers s     ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id

questions.question: For each customer state with at least 1,000 orders, what is the average order value (total payment per order)?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id

SELECT
    c.customer_state                              AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)                    AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2)                        AS total_payments,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 1000
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
questions.note: This excludes canceled and unavailable orders, which also means they don't count toward the 1,000-order threshold, and it uses the payments total (including freight) as the order value.

questions.question: By what percentage did revenue in January–August 2018 grow compared with January–August 2017?
questions.sql:
WITH order_rev AS (
    SELECT o.order_purchase_timestamp AS ts,
           p.payment_value
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND (
            (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-09-01')
         OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01')
      )
),
totals AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(payment_value) FILTER (WHERE ts < '2018-01-01')  AS rev_2017,
        SUM(payment_value) FILTER (WHERE ts >= '2018-01-01') AS rev_2018
    FROM order_rev
)
SELECT
    ROUND(rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2017,
    ROUND(rev_2018, 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2018,
    ROUND((rev_2018 - rev_2017) / rev_2017 * 100, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM totals
questions.note: Revenue here means total payments (SUM of payment_value), excluding canceled and unavailable orders, with each period assigned by purchase date.

questions.question: What was the cancellation rate (percentage of orders canceled) for each month of 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  to_char(date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS orders,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') AS canceled,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancel_rate_pct
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: The rate is canceled orders divided by all orders placed that month, grouped by purchase month; 'unavailable' orders count in the total but not as canceled.

questions.question: For the top 5 product categories by 2017 revenue, what was each category's revenue in January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_sales AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
        ) AS rev_2017,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
        ) AS rev_2018_jan_aug
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_2017,
    ROUND(COALESCE(rev_2018_jan_aug, 0), 2) AS revenue_2018_jan_aug
FROM cat_sales
WHERE rev_2017 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY rev_2017 DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(price) without freight, because the question breaks revenue down by category. Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and categories are ranked by their full-year 2017 revenue.

questions.question: What percentage of item revenue in January–August 2018 came from the 10 products with the highest revenue in that period?
questions.sql:
WITH product_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.product_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY oi.product_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           revenue,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, product_id) AS rn
    FROM product_rev
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(revenue) FILTER (WHERE rn <= 10), 2) AS top10_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) FILTER (WHERE rn <= 10) / SUM(revenue), 2) AS top10_pct
FROM ranked
questions.note: Item revenue is SUM(price) without freight, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded; ties at rank 10 are broken by product_id.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest percentage of late deliveries, among categories with at least 500 delivered orders?
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           (o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),
order_cats AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) AS late_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct
FROM delivered d
JOIN order_cats oc ON oc.order_id = d.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500
ORDER BY late_pct DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: An order with items in several categories counts once toward each of those categories, and products with no category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: How much lower is the average review score for delivered orders that arrived late than for delivered orders that arrived on time?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
delivered AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           (o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late,
           s.score
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_scores s ON s.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(score) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_late), 2) AS on_time_avg_score,
    ROUND(AVG(score) FILTER (WHERE is_late), 2)     AS late_avg_score,
    ROUND(AVG(score) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_late)
        - AVG(score) FILTER (WHERE is_late), 2)     AS score_gap,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_late)             AS on_time_orders,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_late)                 AS late_orders
FROM delivered
questions.note: Scores are first averaged per order, so orders with several reviews count once. Orders with no review are excluded.

questions.question: For each month from January to August 2018, what was the cumulative revenue since the start of 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS monthly_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_revenue
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
questions.note: Revenue here is the default order-level measure: payments (`SUM(payment_value)`). It excludes canceled and unavailable orders and is grouped by purchase month.

questions.question: Show me last year's numbers.
questions.sql:
WITH last_year AS (
    SELECT MAX(date_part('year', order_purchase_timestamp))::int AS yr
    FROM orders
),
sales_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_unique_id
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN last_year ly ON date_part('year', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = ly.yr
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
pay AS (
    SELECT op.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments op
    JOIN sales_orders s ON s.order_id = op.order_id
    GROUP BY op.order_id
),
items AS (
    SELECT oi.order_id,
           COUNT(*)              AS units,
           SUM(oi.price)         AS item_sales,
           SUM(oi.freight_value) AS freight
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN sales_orders s ON s.order_id = oi.order_id
    GROUP BY oi.order_id
)
SELECT
    (SELECT yr FROM last_year)                                        AS year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id)                                        AS orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_unique_id)                              AS unique_customers,
    COALESCE(SUM(i.units), 0)                                         AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2)                                             AS revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(i.item_sales), 2)                                       AS item_sales,
    ROUND(SUM(i.freight), 2)                                          AS freight,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id), 0), 2)     AS avg_order_value
FROM sales_orders s
LEFT JOIN pay   p ON p.order_id = s.order_id
LEFT JOIN items i ON i.order_id = s.order_id
questions.note: I took "last year" to mean the latest year in the data, 2018, and "numbers" to mean headline sales metrics, excluding canceled and unavailable orders. Note that 2018 is incomplete: data effectively runs only from January to August.

questions.question: Which products perform best?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*)                                              AS units_sold,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)                           AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2)                               AS revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)                               AS avg_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_category_name_english
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I took "perform best" to mean the 10 products with the highest item revenue (SUM of price, excluding canceled and unavailable orders), and included units sold and order counts for context.

questions.question: What will our revenue be next month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.payment_value)                                 AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT month,
           revenue,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY month) AS t
    FROM monthly
),
fit AS (
    SELECT regr_slope(revenue::float8, t)     AS slope,
           regr_intercept(revenue::float8, t) AS intercept,
           MAX(t)                             AS last_t
    FROM indexed
)
SELECT DATE '2018-09-01'                                              AS forecast_month,
       ROUND((f.intercept + f.slope * (f.last_t + 1))::numeric, 2)    AS trend_forecast,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(revenue), 2)
          FROM indexed
         WHERE month >= DATE '2018-06-01')                            AS avg_last_3m,
       (SELECT ROUND(revenue, 2)
          FROM indexed
         WHERE month = DATE '2018-08-01')                             AS last_month_actual
FROM fit f
questions.note: This is a simple projection, not a real forecast. It treats "next month" as September 2018, because the data feed effectively ends in August 2018. Revenue means payments from orders that were not canceled or unavailable. The query fits a linear trend over the reliable months (Jan 2017 to Aug 2018) and shows the average of the last three months as a more conservative estimate. Monthly revenue flattened during 2018, so the linear trend probably overstates September.

questions.question: Which product has the most appealing name?
questions.sql:
WITH sales AS (
    SELECT
        oi.product_id,
        COUNT(*)      AS units_sold,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY oi.product_id
)
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    p.product_name_length                                AS name_length,
    s.units_sold,
    ROUND(s.revenue, 2)                                  AS revenue
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = s.product_id
ORDER BY s.units_sold DESC, s.revenue DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note:
The dataset has no product names, only `product_name_length`, so it can't say which name is most appealing. As a stand-in for "appeal", this query returns the best-selling product by units sold, along with its category and name length.

I assumed units sold (excluding canceled and unavailable orders) is a fair proxy for appeal; this measures how popular the product is, not anything about its name.
